proof_details: The strong endpoint unit ball has compact image in each admissible lower norm space, by the verified full Wiener weak dual and AppendixB lower-topology theorem. This proves compactness of the actual strong endpoint inclusion without claiming vanishing infinity tails.
The physical free operator -d^2/dx^2+1 is a proved bounded isomorphism H1 to H-minus-one on the full original distribution spaces, with reciprocal symbol1/(1+pi^2*k^2).

Endpoint multiplication on the entire H1 domain lands in the original endpoint space, whose H-minus-one inclusion is compact. The domain inclusion is also compact. The fixed free normalization of L(q)-lambda is therefore identity plus compact at every lambda.

Verified shared Fredholm theory gives index zero, finite-dimensional physical eigenspaces and bijectivity from injectivity; shared analytic Schur theory provides a local analytic determinant at every parameter. No physical algebraic-multiplicity identity is inferred from this local determinant.

The existing high-strip determinant criterion is upgraded from the physical point eigen-equation to full operator pencil invertibility. A concrete point pi^2*n^2+i*n is proved to be in the resolvent set at each admissible large mode.

The total ring inverse of the normalized pencil defines a bounded inverse from all original H-minus-one right-hand sides into original H1. Both inverse identities, the full physical resolvent identity and local norm analyticity are proved on the actual resolvent set.

Composition with the original domain inclusion gives the actual compact base-space resolvent. Its closed-equation characterization proves closedness of the physical graph and closedness of the standard LinearPMap operator.

Every physical eigenvalue lambda becomes the eigenvalue1/(lambda-a) of one actual compact base resolvent. The shared finite-eigenvalues-away-from-zero theorem proves that every bounded spectral region has finitely many actual physical spectral values.
